description:
Every campaign receipt records the host governor, SMT state and load, but not the scheduling priority the timed processes achieved, so a change in that priority shifts measurements without any record flagging it.

## Background

The CCX1 lock wrapper requests `nice -n -5` as a best-effort pin. On the benchmark host the process nice limit is 0, so the request is refused, GNU `nice` warns and runs the command anyway, and every committed campaign since 2026-05-27 ran at niceness 0. The measurements are mutually comparable, and the gap is one of provenance: on a host where the pin succeeds, or after a limit change, timed work runs at a different priority and the receipt's host observation records nothing about it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each session host observation in a receipt records the achieved scheduling priority of the timed process, read at run time from the process itself rather than from the requested value.
- [hard] REQ-02: The acceptance evaluator treats sessions of one campaign whose achieved priority differs as a recorded finding, and campaigns with a uniform priority evaluate to the verdict they evaluate to before this change.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every existing committed receipt evaluates to its committed verdict after the change, shown by a committed re-evaluation record.

## Notes

The wrapper's own comment already calls the pin best-effort; that stays. No frozen addendum or committed receipt changes.
title: Record the achieved scheduling priority in receipt host observations
